headline: Ship a notebook-first, honestly labelled NucleiSky example now: images and numbers precomputed by running the RELEASED NucleiSky code (0.1.1, identical to main) on the seeded fixture, native layer controls only, no matcher control, no re-drawn desktop apps. Then add stamped real captures (which also verify the numbers), then a 75-90 s user video. napari/Fiji views wait on facts outside this repository.

decisions.question: Which example leads, and from which code path do the numbers come?
decisions.decision: NucleiSky 2D registration on the make_nucleisky.py fixture (1600x1600 reference at 0.65 um/px, 520x520 query at 0.325 um/px, 12 degree rotation, seeded; fixture sha256 2f3e168d / 67ed77fc / 14b8f149 verified stable across library sets). The generator calls the code that exists in release tag 0.1.1 (src and notebooks are identical to origin/main c8f8735), with 'threshold' segmentation (429 and 9 nuclei) and the default config, through the entry point the notebook uses. example.json records the entry point, config, commit and tag, library versions, and whatever that code prints. The earlier screenshot numbers (12.1721, 1.0024, 700.3293 / 605.5654, matcher quad) came from the unmerged bridge-test tool function (78c7f0a) and are NOT shown unless the released path reproduces them; a direct call on main gave scale about 1.0020 and offsets about 700.17 / 605.29 px, same bbox rows 637-963 and columns 597-923, rotation about 12.17.
decisions.reason: Both reviewers showed the draft sold bridge-test numbers as the released product. The page may only show what 0.1.1 can produce. Stage 2 then compares against the real installed notebook; if its numbers differ, example.json is regenerated, never hand-edited.

decisions.question: What is interactive, given that nothing may be fabricated?
decisions.decision: Only native controls that switch between stored views of one real result: three layer checkboxes (reference, aligned small image, footprint outline), an opacity range for the aligned layer (with aria-valuetext), and a radio 'View: whole field / zoom to the footprint'. The matching-method radio is REMOVED. No <button>, no Run, no upload. The control fieldsets carry the hidden attribute in static HTML and demo.js removes it, so without JavaScript there are no dead controls.
decisions.reason: The matcher states (triangles and graph failing, quad-only, hashing, 'Matcher = auto' wording) exist only in the unmerged bridge-tool code; on released code graph succeeds when given features and the released notebook has no Matcher dropdown (Option A runs all four, Option B uses an automatic order). Showing the control would invent a feature of the installed app. Hidden-until-JS fixes the 'inert controls' problem the plan itself criticises in re-drawn UIs.

decisions.question: Re-draw JupyterLab, napari and Fiji windows in HTML/CSS (spec C)?
decisions.decision: No. Stage 1 draws no host UI. Stage 2 adds stamped real captures of the installed app. napari/Fiji appear only as one derived sentence plus a link until Stage 4 preconditions are met.
decisions.reason: Look-alike UIs decay silently, create dead focusable controls, copy Linux/Xvfb artefacts, imply napari/Fiji parity that NucleiSky's manifest (hosts [notebook]) denies, and the real notebook (Steps 0-3, Option A/B, hidden code cells, new-tab open) does not match the spec's invented five steps.

decisions.question: Staging
decisions.decision: Stage 1 launch page and tile (developer only, plus consent and wording review). Stage 2 real captures (needs a person on a real desktop; also the external check of the numbers). Stage 3 user video 75-90 s. Stage 4 host views, conditional on external preconditions. Each stage has a go/no-go gate, and gates are labelled CI-enforced or manual.
decisions.reason: Different readers and decay rates; the video must reuse Stage 2 frames or it would show things nobody has captured.

decisions.question: Where do numbers, wording and images live (single source of truth)?
decisions.decision: Offline generator tools/demo_assets/ (Python 3.12) writes content/demo/media/* and content/demo/example.json (outputs, settings, footprint polygon corners, derived comparison to the known transform, fixture sha256, source commit SHAs and release tag, library versions, display-processing record such as 8-bit windowing, sha256 of every committed media file). data/demo.yaml holds wording, alt texts, tile text only. Python renders the table, status strings and the footprint SVG from example.json at build time; JS only toggles. The site build never imports numpy or scipy. Media are committed vendored artefacts; docs/assets/demo and docs/demo are generated and git-ignored.
decisions.reason: No second hand-maintained description; numbers are never retyped in HTML, JS or YAML. Hand edits of media fail the hash test.

decisions.question: How is the generator pinned and run, and what does CI enforce?
decisions.decision: tools/demo_assets/requirements.txt pins Python 3.12 and NucleiSky's own pins (numpy 2.0.2, numba 0.60.0) plus pandas (imported at module top by pipeline.py), networkx (graph matcher), scipy, tifffile, scikit-image, matplotlib, Pillow; NucleiSky is installed from the pinned commit; 'threshold' segmentation means torch and cellpose are not needed (verified: uv venv, installs in about 3 s). CI (unit tests, post-build checks) enforces only: committed media sha256 equals example.json, fixture hashes and source SHAs and tag present, schema valid. CI never runs the generator. A documented manual regeneration check (README, optionally a workflow_dispatch job later) compares fixture hashes exactly and numeric outputs within tolerance; media bytes are NOT expected to be reproducible across machines.
decisions.reason: publish.yml installs only the site requirements and runs unit tests first; JPEG/PNG/matplotlib bytes differ across encoders and versions, but fixture TIFF hashes are stable.

decisions.question: Where does the HTML live, how does it stay accessible, and how does it render without JavaScript?
decisions.decision: pages_demo.py (plus pages_demo_viewer.py) builds the page (layout wide, menu guides/, crumb '<- Docs', no Docs sidebar). One balanced root <section data-demo>. Without JS the reader sees a stacked list of real figures (reference, small image, overlay composite), each with its own caption and real alt text, the table and the QC figure; controls are hidden. With JS the viewer block appears: a single div role=img whose aria-label JS updates per state, with the layer images aria-hidden and alt='' inside it, loading=eager (finish_site would otherwise add loading=lazy and hidden layers would flash blank); the footprint outline is an inline SVG polygon (stroke at least 2 px at display size, vector-effect non-scaling-stroke) generated from the corners in example.json. A role=status line carries the meaning: position, rotation, and the share of the field the small image covers, all derived from example.json. Controls are at least 44 px high, fieldset+legend, one checked radio per group.
decisions.reason: check_design forces a real alt on every in main, which would make a screen reader read stacked layers as separate pictures; a narrow, tested exemption inside the viewer role=img container is cleaner than weakening the global rule. Non-JS readers get meaning without controls.

decisions.question: How is 2D_QC.jpg handled, and how is the QC figure explained?
decisions.decision: 2D_QC.jpg is not used. The QC figure is regenerated from the fixture with the notebook's own plotting call at the same code commit (so it is one code path with the numbers) and shown with its real SSIM values. Caption: 'SSIM is computed over the whole exported region, including the margin and corners the small image does not cover, where the warped image is zero. The first-row score is therefore low even though the overlay is good. The small image is also a resampled, noisy, gain-changed copy, which lowers SSIM too.' The caption does not claim the region is 'much larger' (326x326 px is about 1.6 times the footprint area).
decisions.reason: 2D_QC.jpg is another dataset with unstated provenance. Cropping the low SSIM would alter real output; over-explaining one cause would be wrong.

decisions.question: How are the result rows labelled so they cannot be misread?
decisions.decision: Table groups: Inputs (sizes, pixel sizes, nucleus counts), Settings used (segmentation method threshold/Otsu, blur sigma, min area, watershed, peak distance, seed, adaptive matching; all from example.json; plus the sentence 'The notebook's default segmentation is Cellpose; other settings give slightly different values'), Result (rotation, scale with note, offset, export region), Check (difference from the known transform, labelled 'computed by this site, not a NucleiSky output'). Offset row: 'Row / column in reference pixels of the small image's top-left corner' with a second derived row 'Centre of the small image, computed by this site: row ..., column ...'. Export-region row: 'Region exported for the QC figure (includes a margin), rows 637-963, columns 597-923 (row = y, column = x)'; the drawn outline is separately called 'footprint drawn from the recovered transform' and a test asserts it lies inside the export region. Scale note: 'Scale is the physical scale; both images cover the same physical size, so it is about 1.' Pixel sizes note: 'The small image was made by resampling the reference at twice the pixel density; it contains no extra detail.' Ground truth shown only as the Check row (rotation and position difference, generator-computed) and 'Rotation used to make the test image: 12 degrees (for checking, not a result)'. No run duration.
decisions.reason: Reviewer 2 showed the draft's bbox, offsets, 'sampled twice as finely' and missing settings were each misleading to a skeptic; the generator already knows the errors, so show them instead of a cherry-picked rotation row.

decisions.question: Citation and scientific-claim placement
decisions.decision: The manifest doi row comes after the synthetic notice and never beside the result, with the sentence: 'This synthetic example does not reproduce the paper's results; the paper evaluates real images.' The page never says or implies cross-scale multimodal registration is demonstrated.
decisions.reason: A self-crop of one synthetic field with 9 query nuclei is the easiest case.

decisions.question: What if NucleiSky is absent from the snapshot or has no release?
decisions.decision: Policy written in AGENTS.md and implemented in demo_media.app_state(): on pull-request and push builds fail() with a message naming registry/CellMigrationLab__NucleiSky.yaml. On scheduled builds (distinguished by the mechanism the build already uses for left-out apps; if none exists, GITHUB_EVENT_NAME == 'schedule', unverified) the page and tile are still built from example.json (so using-apps.md, llms.txt and tile links never go dead), the app-linked rows (app page link, manifest doi, release line) are replaced by the visible line 'NucleiSky is currently not listed in the App Centre', and a WARNING is printed. Tests cover app-missing and release-missing for both modes.
decisions.reason: One broken app must never take the daily build down, and silent omission would break 'no silent fallbacks'; keeping the page avoids dead links from static Markdown that cannot be conditionally removed.

decisions.question: Staleness warning: how is it raised and how does it reach a person?
decisions.decision: The recorded code release tag (example.json) is compared with the snapshot's latest NucleiSky release; on difference build_site prints 'WARNING: /demo/ was precomputed with NucleiSky <x>; latest release is <y>' to stderr in the same style as guides.py:190, formatted as a GitHub Actions ::warning:: annotation so it shows on the run summary. Frames (Stage 2) get a six-month review date with the same warning after it. build/problems.md is NOT used: only the fetch stage writes it (catalogue.py:143-149) and the 'Report left-out apps' step reads it before pages are generated. No issue is opened automatically; that limit is stated in AGENTS.md.
decisions.reason: The draft pointed at a file the build never writes; the release-keyed check is meaningful now that the numbers come from a tagged release.

decisions.question: Video: length, audience, hosting, narration
decisions.decision: One user video of 75-90 s built from Stage 2 captures: 150-190 words (Piper measured about 159 words per minute, so 190-225 words would exceed the cap). Self-hosted MP4 (H.264, 720p, CRF 26-28, AAC 64 kbps mono, faststart) plus a WebM VP9 test encode for in-container Chromium (which cannot decode H.264); <video controls preload=none poster>, caption track set default, short burned-in on-screen labels so muted viewing works, transcript with a per-scene visual description (Missing Metadata card, typed pixel sizes, numbers on screen) and a statement if the voice is synthetic; no autoplay, no YouTube. Size cap 10 MB enforced in the build. Narration: a person if available, otherwise Piper en_US-ljspeech-high (public domain claim to be confirmed on the voice's model card, unverified) or en_US-libritts_r-medium (CC BY, credited); never lessac. Playback is checked on GitHub Pages (Range support; the local server has none).
decisions.reason: 260-300 words cannot carry eight topics; self-hosting avoids the site's first third-party request; transcripts from VTT alone omit on-screen facts.

decisions.question: Requirements and install facts on the page and in the video
decisions.decision: Stage 1 page states system requirements taken from NucleiSky's own docs/release (disk space, GPU optional but slower for the default Cellpose, macOS support) with the install time labelled 'typical for a small app; NucleiSky is large'. Intel Mac is not passed over silently: the 0.1.1 release lists MacOSX-x86_64 .pkg/.sh assets while the Tools protocol says Intel Macs are unsupported for NucleiSky. Until the authors answer, the page says 'Apple Silicon Macs' and the question goes to the authors. Actual release asset sizes are read from the release at generation time.
decisions.reason: The draft hid facts that would make a visitor's install fail (about 25 GB free and 9 GB installed were reported; unverified here).

decisions.question: Host views (napari, Fiji, QuPath)
decisions.decision: Out of Stage 1-3. One sentence, built from the NucleiSky manifest hosts: when hosts == [notebook]: 'NucleiSky runs in a notebook today and is not available in napari, Fiji or QuPath yet. Plugins that bring apps into those programs are a prototype; their guide says they are "untested and unlikely to be stable".' with a link to /guides/image-software/. If hosts ever differ, a generic 'see the app page for supported programs' text is used and a WARNING is printed, so a person re-reads the wording. At build time the quoted phrase is asserted to exist in the fetched image-software guide (currently docs/guides/image-software/index.md:142), else fail() naming that file. Authoritative statement is the image-software guide; the other site statements (data/site.yaml:8, pages_site.py page_home, cards.py:64) are reconciled in the same pull request or this sentence defers to them.
decisions.reason: NucleiSky's Relocalize 2D exists only on unmerged bridge-test; hard-coded quotes drift silently.

decisions.question: Is the Playground Feature tour used?
decisions.decision: Not as the front door. Preferred Stage 4 candidate (ships tools on main, release 0.0.1, hosts notebook/napari/fiji/qupath), conditional on a notebook cell and real captures.
decisions.reason: Fully precomputable but a test fixture on synthetic discs, no screenshots, no notebook step, listed under 'Testing and maintenance'.

decisions.question: Design-rule changes: scope
decisions.decision: Narrow, bound to <main>: 'Inside <main>, input type radio, checkbox or range is allowed only inside a data-demo root.' Header, drawer, search and menu controls (md-toggle __drawer, md-toggle __search, lc-menu-toggle, App Centre search/select) are untouched. New module scripts/check_design_demo.py (about 170 lines, own HTMLParser with a nesting stack) called from check_design.py through a small raw-HTML pass (about 10-15 lines, since check_design.main holds only Facts objects). Failure tests: range input in main outside the root fails; the theme's header checkboxes are not flagged; root without notice fails; layer imgs with empty alt outside the viewer container still fail; hidden-until-JS fieldsets are the only allowed pattern.
decisions.reason: There is no existing input rule, so this is a new restriction scoped to main; DESIGN.md must change first and the gate must stay strict.

decisions.question: Home tile and other entry points
decisions.decision: One secondary card-link band after the comic. Text from data/demo.yaml; image is the overlay composite JPEG (RGB, so images.shrink works; alpha PNGs cannot go through it) with required alt. One sentence in content/guides/using-apps.md, a line in llms.txt. No sixth top-menu entry, no Use-hub card.
decisions.reason: The hero's two entry cards must not be outranked; reuse existing generation paths.

decisions.question: Exposure and launch
decisions.decision: Do not flip extra.listed. Notify the NucleiSky authors (consent preferred) before merge; flipping listed is a separate launch decision.
decisions.reason: The page describes someone else's app; the site is unlisted (noindex).

decisions.question: Where do demo.js and demo.css live and how are they loaded?
decisions.decision: Committed in docs/assets/javascripts/demo.js (at most 120 lines) and docs/assets/stylesheets/demo.css (at most 150 lines, scoped under .lc-demo), next to the existing hand-written assets; only generated media go to GENERATED docs/assets/demo. overrides/main.html gets guarded blocks (about 5 lines): {% if page.meta and page.meta.page_css %} link in extrahead; {% block scripts %}{{ super() }}{% if page.meta and page.meta.page_js %} script {% endif %}{% endblock %}. Unguarded 'or []' loops raise 'undefined value'; omitting super() drops the theme bundle. Instant navigation is off, so the script runs once per load. 300 lines per hand-written JS/CSS file is a reviewed convention (lc.css is already 338); tests add a size and [hidden] check for demo files.
decisions.reason: Nothing copies content/ subfolders into docs/; this avoids a new copy step and a second location convention. Reviewer 1 verified the guarded template form.

corrected_facts: Draft claim 'reproduced the screenshot numbers to every printed digit' holds only for the unmerged bridge-test tool function (78c7f0a). On released code (0.1.1 == main src and notebooks, c8f8735) a default NucleiSky() call gives bbox rows 637-963 / columns 597-923 and rotation about 12.17, but scale 1.00204 (quad and hashing), translation 455.107 / 393.437 um = 700.17 / 605.29 px, not 1.0024 and 700.3293 / 605.5654. The generator therefore regenerates the displayed numbers from the released path.

Draft claim 'quad and hashing succeed; triangles and graph show No match found' is bridge-test only. Tag 0.1.1 is an ancestor of origin/bridge-test; git diff 0.1.1 origin/main -- src notebooks is empty; bridge-test adds the matcher_order argument to run_adaptive_matching_and_export in pipeline.py/segmentation.py. On released code graph succeeded when given features. The released notebook has no 'Matcher' dropdown, so the 'Matcher = auto' notice refers to a label that does not exist there. The matcher radio is dropped.

The bbox [637, 963, 597, 923] (326x326 px) is the export and QC region of interest with a margin (export.py bbox_full_px_from_similarity_um with margin_um), not the small image's footprint (tight rotated footprint about 646-954 by 606-914). Offsets are the pixel position of the small image's top-left corner after rotation (centre about row 800, column 760), listed as row then column.

The small image is a bilinear resampling (zoom 2.0, plus gain and noise) of the same synthetic array; 'sampled twice as finely' wrongly suggested a finer acquisition. The demo does not support the paper's cross-scale multimodal claim.

The recorded numbers came from otsu thresholding, sigma 1.0, watershed on, peak distance 5, min area 5 (tool) versus 80 (notebook), whereas the notebook defaults to Cellpose; other settings gave 12.2927 / 425 nuclei (li) and 12.1876 / 378 (no watershed). Settings must be shown.

SSIM is low in the first row because it is computed over the whole ROI with warp mode constant, cval 0 (area outside the footprint scores low); the ROI is only about 1.6 times the footprint area, not 'much larger', and the noisy gain-changed copy also lowers SSIM.

Correction to the draft's own file list: the poster rewriting gap is at scripts/lcsite/page.py:85 (re.sub(r'\b(href|src)=...'); page.py has 93 lines), not :268. scripts/check_site.py:56 is correct. The gap itself is confirmed: neither fix_links nor check_site look at poster.

build/problems.md is written only by scripts/lcsite/catalogue.py:143-149; build_site.py never writes it and the 'Report left-out apps' workflow step reads it before 'Generate pages'. The existing build-time warning pattern is a stderr print (guides.py:190).

Every built page has checkboxes outside <main> (md-toggle __drawer, md-toggle __search, lc-menu-toggle) and the App Centre has input type=search and a <select>; check_design has no rule against inputs today, so the demo rule is a new restriction that must be scoped to <main>, not an exemption.

pipeline.py imports pandas at module top and the graph matcher needs networkx; NucleiSky pins numpy 2.0.2 and numba 0.60.0, which need Python 3.12 or older (container python3 and the site .venv are 3.13). Cellpose/torch are only lazily needed, not for the 'threshold' method.

Media sizes measured on the real fixture with Pillow: reference whole 800 px JPEG q80 47 KB, zoomed reference 29 KB, query 13 KB, aligned layer as 800x800 RGB JPEG on black about 9 KB (but as RGBA PNG 46 KB whole and 170 KB zoomed), outline PNG 4 KB; with the QC figure about 390 KB total in the PNG design. Using JPEG layers with mix-blend-mode: screen and an SVG outline, the budget is a measured figure of roughly 250-300 KB; the generator reports the real total and a test caps it.

finish_site.lazy_images adds loading=lazy to every in
that lacks a loading attribute (IMG regex), so hidden layer images would not load until first shown; layer images need explicit loading=eager and an Images exception in DESIGN.md.

The bundled Chromium reports canPlayType('') for avc1/mp4a (VP9/WebM is 'probably'); the local preview server has no Range support (200, no Accept-Ranges). Piper works in the container (piper-tts 1.8.0 in a 3.12 venv, ljspeech-high 114 MB): 12 words took 4.5 s, about 159 wpm, so 190-225 words is 72-85 s of speech before pauses.
check_design_demo.py realistically needs 150-190 lines and pages_demo 200 lines (viewer helpers split into pages_demo_viewer.py); the check_design hook is not '+4 lines'.

Unit tests run before fetch and build in CI and Page.write() writes to the real docs/ with no output-root parameter, so built-page assertions cannot be unit tests. They belong in the post-build check step; Playwright audits are in no workflow and are a manual pre-launch gate.

Release 0.1.1 contains MacOSX-x86_64 .pkg and .sh assets, while the Tools protocol says Intel Macs are unsupported for NucleiSky; the draft's 'do not mention Intel Mac' was wrong. The '6-8 minute install' comes from the generic template doc, not this roughly 9 GB app.

The draft's host wording 'Experimental integration, currently under testing' is wrong; the bridge guides say 'Under heavy construction ... untested and unlikely to be stable' (docs/guides/image-software/index.md:142 on the site), tested on Linux only, Windows .bat hooks never run on real Windows, macOS untested.

Where a reviewer was NOT followed: (a) the 4-of-5 biologist comprehension check stays as a pre-launch target for the launch decision, not a merge gate, and may be replaced by a smaller documented check or a documented waiver if participants cannot be recruited; it is no longer coupled to a 'rerun until it passes' loop. (b) The reviewer's option to omit the demo page when NucleiSky is missing on scheduled builds was replaced by keep-with-degraded-rows, because static Markdown links (using-apps.md) and llms.txt cannot be conditionally removed without dead links; pull-request builds still fail.

NucleiSky's Relocalize 2D (and the other bridge tools) exist only on unmerged branch bridge-test (28 commits ahead). NucleiSky main's manifest says hosts [notebook]; release 0.1.1 (2026-07-07) predates the bridge. Only Playground (main, release 0.0.1) and GuessTheCondition (release 0.0.0) ship host tools; CellTracksColab only on a branch; VLab4Mic unverified.

'The installer registers the application' is true only for apps with their own post-install hook; the hook is not in template main (v0.1.15) but on the template's unmerged bridge-test branch. labconstrictor-tools and napari-labconstrictor return 404 on PyPI, Fiji has no update site, no host plugin has a release.

NucleiSky2DApp is Step 0 (initialise), Step 1 (load images and extract features), Step 2 (matching, Option A ' Run NucleiSky2D' or Option B ' Run adaptive NucleiSky2D', QC plots inside), Step 3 (apply saved transform). Real buttons: ' Load & Process', ' Run Segmentation', ' Run NucleiSky2D'. Vocabulary is Full/Crop, napari and Fiji say Reference/Query. No example data ships and no 'select included example' control exists; the fixture TIFFs carry no pixel-size metadata, so the real notebook shows a red 'Missing Metadata' card and 0.65 / 0.325 must be typed in. 'Generate Random Crop' cannot reproduce exactly 12 degrees and 2x.

'Open the notebook' in the Welcome notebook opens a new browser tab; the hidden code cell must be run first; the launcher also opens a terminal that must stay open. The Welcome notebook contains a GitHub token flow that must not be mimicked; there is no 'Test Connection' button.

Welcome_Notebook.png on doc_source is outdated ('Welcome to NotebookApp!'); the site's existing alt text ('orange Open the Notebook button') is wrong: headers are orange, the button is blue. hubs.yaml calls the N2 napari picture 'a test app' but it shows NucleiSky Relocalize 2D from a branch.

The napari/Fiji screenshots are Linux/Xvfb widget grabs (napari 0.9.2 with a PyQt5 deprecation toast, Fiji 2.18, Java 21), older than bridge-test HEAD; napari's default post-run view is a black canvas with 9 dots; Fiji's result is a separate RGB window; napari's two dropdowns have no visible labels.
2D_QC.jpg is a different real dataset (SSIM 0.305 and 0.995), not an interface and not the fixture; provenance and licence unstated.

Fixture generation needs numpy, scipy and tifffile and is deterministic. The query holds only 9 detected nuclei; synthetic Gaussian blobs; exact overlap shows white so an outline is needed. Playground notebook has no Feature tour cell; its README 'blobs in two parts' is false (14 discs plus 2 rings).

Storyboard wording: the manifest has doi and docs_url, not 'citation', and does not list an app (the author must submit a public repo). Pinned versions come from requirements.yaml. Release installers are not code-signed. A two-minute narration holds only 260-300 words.

Site facts: <video> and <track> pass check_design silently; check_design allows content buttons only for copy and clear-filters; the Docs menu highlight needs front matter menu: guides/ (verified, aria-current on Docs, check_site menu rule passes); AGENTS.md Navigation paragraph says every guide page shows the docs sidebar, which the demo (no sidebar) does not.

Local clones are stale (template working tree 31 files behind origin/main; NucleiSky checkout lacked labconstrictor-app.yaml). Read origin/main or the GitHub tools when verifying anything for this plan.

stages.name: Stage 1: Precomputed example page and home tile (smallest launch-worthy stage)
stages.goal: A newcomer sees the task (find where a small image sits in a larger one using the pattern of nuclei), sees real results produced by NucleiSky's released code, can toggle stored views of that one result, and cannot mistake it for a live app, an upload tool, a recording of an app session, or a validated napari/Fiji integration.
deliverables: tools/demo_assets generator (Python 3.12, pinned stack, pinned NucleiSky commit that equals tag 0.1.1 code) writing media plus example.json with entry point, settings, outputs, footprint corners, derived difference from the known transform, display-processing record, hashes, SHAs, tag, versions, release asset sizes

content/demo/media: reference 800x800 JPEG, small image, aligned layer as RGB JPEG on black (screen blending), whole-field and zoomed views, overlay composite JPEG (also the tile image), QC figure from the notebook's own plotting call; measured total reported and capped (about 250-300 KB), no TIFFs

/demo/ page: task sentence; precomputed notice inside the figure frame; no-JS stacked figures; JS viewer (role=img, layer checkboxes, opacity range, view radio, SVG outline, role=status with text equivalent); table with Inputs, Settings used, Result, Check groups and the exact row labels; scale and pixel-size notes; QC figure with the corrected SSIM caption; requirements and install facts; citation row after the notice with the 'does not reproduce the paper's results' sentence; derived host sentence; provenance and display-processing line; links to app page, install guide, notebook guide, image-software guide
App-missing and release-missing policy (fail on PR builds, degraded rows plus warning on scheduled builds)
Staleness stderr/::warning:: line keyed to the recorded release tag
Home tile, using-apps sentence, llms.txt line
hubs.yaml alt-text fixes (Welcome picture: blue button under orange headers; napari picture: NucleiSky Relocalize 2D prototype)
Narrow design-rule change with DESIGN.md/AGENTS.md/README.md edited together
Tests: pure-function unit tests plus post-build checks with leakage and failure cases

labconstrictor-site: content/demo/media/*, content/demo/example.json (about 6-8 KB), content/demo/example.schema.json (about 60 lines; includes the exact recorded notices if any)

risks: Numbers differ between the released-code generator and the real installed notebook (library versions, entry point, defaults). Mitigation: example.json records entry point and config; Stage 2 compares against the real notebook and regenerates if needed. Until then the 'Precomputed by NucleiSky's code, not a recording of an app session' wording stays.

Build fragility around NucleiSky for the daily scheduled build (app missing, no release, hosts changed): handled by the explicit PR-fail versus scheduled-degrade policy, warnings and tests; the warning reaches a person only via the run log and annotation (no issue opened).

Synthetic blobs look like a toy; the small image has only 9 nuclei and is a resampled self-crop, the easiest case. Mitigation: explicit notices, the paper-claim disclaimer and settings block; a real, licensed image would replace it by re-running the generator.
Low SSIM on a visually good overlay confuses visitors; shown and explained with the corrected caption, not cropped.
A viewer may be read as 'upload and run here'. Mitigation: no upload, no Run, notice inside the figure frame, hidden-until-JS controls, comprehension question in the pre-launch check.

Screen-reader behaviour of the role=img viewer with aria-hidden layers and the empty-alt exemption is unverified; needs a manual screen-reader pass. The layer images' eager loading adds a few hundred KB on a page the visitor chose.
Design-gate erosion: exemption bound to a data-demo root inside main with failure tests; never relax the global button/alt checks.

Vendored artefacts go stale: hashes, provenance, release-keyed warning and a six-month frame review date; host UI drift cannot be detected, only dated. No CI step runs the generator; drift is only caught by the manual check (an optional workflow_dispatch job can be added).
Estimate risk: 7-10 days assumes the pinned 3.12 stack installs as reviewed; checker size (about 170 lines) and viewer split into two modules are planned so no file nears 300.

Video: weight is motion-driven (3-12 MB), repeated re-encodes inflate git history; bundled Chromium cannot decode H.264 and the preview server lacks Range support; Piper is GPL-3.0 (build tool only), lessac voice is research-licensed, libritts_r needs CC BY credit, ljspeech public-domain status to be confirmed; a synthetic voice must be disclosed.
